history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration complete its review of the fuel category strategy in a timely manner to adapt it to various challenges, including by exploring additional contract tools and operating models in order to reduce its dependence on a very limited number of suppliers.
history.administration_response: The recommendation is under implementation. Review of the fuel category strategy is in progress, with the aim of reducing dependency on limited suppliers. As part of the review, the Office of Supply Chain Management will hold two vendor outreach events (vendor round tables) in Mogadishu and Mombasa, Kenya from 28 October to 1 November 2024 in order to gather input from the market on how best to structure missions’ petroleum oil and lubricant supply and services requirements. The forums will also be used to create awareness on the business opportunities, United Nations petroleum oil and lubricant requirements, how requirements are defined in scopes of work and the use of bid response tables. This is expected to help vendors to produce quality technical proposals. The strategy will be revised further and approved after incorporating, as required, feedback received from participants of the planned vendor round tables.
history.board_assessment: The Board acknowledges the efforts made. Once the strategy is finalized and published, the recommendation will be considered implemented.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration complete its review of the fuel category strategy in a timely manner to adapt it to various challenges, including by exploring additional contract tools and operating models in order to reduce its dependence on a very limited number of suppliers.
history.administration_response: The Department of Operational Support/Office of Supply Chain Management continues work to implement a comprehensive approach to mitigate identified risks in the fuel category. In doing so, a new fuel category strategy has been developed, moving from turn-key models to a split-supply chain approach separating bulk fuel supply from operations and maintenance services. In parallel, efforts regarding vendor outreach and market feedback analysis are under way in order to expand supplier participation. The new strategy development has resulted in pilot solicitations, which demonstrate early results of improved vendor response. However, owing to the timeline for completion of the commercial evaluation, this will require additional time, thereby extending target completion to the first quarter of 2026. These measures will strengthen resilience and reduce the dependency on limited suppliers.
history.board_assessment: The Board acknowledges the progress made and will assess the finalized fuel strategy when it is published. Until then, the recommendation remains under implementation.
